analysis.title: Weekly HF Highlights: De-Grossing Persists as Net Lev Rises 5%; Risk-Off Tone Persists
key_insights: US L/S funds raised net leverage 5% week over week to 51% (45th percentile since 2010), just below longer-term averages. Gross leverage fell 1% to 207% (92nd percentile since 2010).
The majority of the week's buying came from short covers rather than long adds, which the desk reads as hedge funds staying in a risk-off state.

Hedge funds have trimmed gross exposure to global equities steadily since the start of October. Combined with summer de-grossing from which gross never fully recovered, this is the largest stretch of L/S de-grossing in 15+ years.
Funds were net buyers of all regions and covers led the buying in every region. Only Japan saw long adds.
In North America, index-level products drove much of the buying as funds unwound broad short-side hedges. Single-name flow was much more muted.
Tech was the only sector with outsized buying, mostly short covers. Memory, Agentic AI Beneficiaries, Internet and Cybersecurity saw the largest demand within TMT.
Hedge funds were small net sellers of Hyperscalers, with much of the supply on Thursday after several key earnings announcements.

Hedge fund exposure to the AI trade (constituents of the MSXXAI Index) is now underweight relative to US equity market weight for the first time since early 2023. The desk suggests supply from hedge funds in the space may be in its later stages.
Outside TMT, funds sold most other single-name sectors, led by Energy, Materials and Real Estate.

Factor flows: many trends of the last ~2 months reversed. Funds were small net buyers of Momentum and Volatility (net exposure near ~18-month lows) and net sellers of Quality and Size (net exposure at local peaks).

APAC: funds turned net buyers of select countries, with Japan and South Korea the largest share. Buying was driven by covers, with some long demand for Asia Memory names, one of the first long additions in the space in months.
EU equities were bought in much smaller amounts because covering was almost fully offset by long sales, with de-grossing across all sectors.
October performance remains weak. The average global hedge fund gained ~50bps on the week and global L/S funds ~90bps, but they are down -1.7% and -2.2% month to date.

The average Americas-based L/S fund gained ~1.3% on the week, in line with the S&P 500. It is -1.7% MTD vs the S&P 500 +1.0%, a wider gap than July. YTD it is +6.6%, just under half of the S&P 500's +13.8%.
EU-based L/S funds are -1.7% MTD and Asia-based L/S funds -4.0% MTD, after each gaining ~40-50bps on the week.
Crowded longs outperformed in all three regions this week, but the desk says that outperformance appeared to be unwinding on Friday.
Top 50 crowding spread (longs minus shorts) in North America: WTD +0.5%, MTD -4.4%, YTD +18.2%.
